claim: Al Fahidi Historical Neighbourhood (Al Bastakiya) is a free-to-enter restored wind-tower district with narrow lanes, art galleries, museums and cafes, one of Dubai's oldest areas.
quote: Al Fahidi Historical Neighbourhood... one of the oldest heritage sites in Dubai... narrow lanes, wind towers, art galleries, museums and cafes

claim: Entry to Al Fahidi Historical District itself is free; only individual attractions inside charge fees.
quote: Entering the Al Fahidi Historical District is absolutely free, allowing visitors to freely explore its winding alleyways and admire the traditional architecture without incurring any entrance fees.

claim: Al Shindagha Museum is open daily 10:00-20:00 (last entry 19:00) and charges AED 50 for adults, with free entry for children under 5.
Traditional wooden abra boats cross Dubai Creek between Bur Dubai and Deira for AED 1-2 per one-way trip, running from early morning to midnight.
quote: Abra Creek Crossing at Dubai Creek

claim: Abra fares are AED 1-2 per crossing; the Deira Old Souk station gives direct access to the Gold Souk and Spice Souk, and boats accept cash, nol and cards.
quote: All rides except one specific roundtrip route cost AED 2 for a one-way single trip... Cash, nol, debit and credit cards are the modes of payment

claim: SMCCU cultural meals run 1.5 hours with Emirati presenters: Breakfast AED 130 (Mon & Wed 9am), Brunch AED 130 (Fri-Sun 10:30am), Lunch AED 145 (Mon-Thu 1pm), Fuala tea AED 150 (Tue 1pm), Dinner AED 160 (Tue 6:30pm); children under 7 free.
quote: Breakfast: AED 130... Lunch: AED 145... Dinner: AED 160... The experience lasts 1.5 hours... discussions led by our expert Emirati Cultural Presenters

claim: The Coffee Museum sits in a restored wind-tower house in Al Fahidi with free admission, antique brewing equipment, demonstrations and an on-site cafe serving qahwa.
The Coffee Museum at Villa 44 Al Fahidi opens Saturday-Thursday 9:00-17:00, closed Fridays, with free general admission.
Deira's Gold Souk is among the world's largest gold markets and the adjacent Spice Souk sells saffron, frankincense and dried goods; both are free to wander and haggling is expected.
quote: Souks in Dubai: 2026 Guide to Gold, Spice & More
